reasons: A1: The final paper correctly admits that no matched quality comparison exists; released effort and review controls do not establish measured quality improvement.

A2: The governed delivery method, deterministic rescoring and documented accessibility adaptation are credible original applications, but deployed-model identity and comparative uplift remain unproved.
A3: Training, reusable prompts, two reported quarters and development controls support an adaptability narrative; longitudinal use and reviewed-output quality records are absent.
A4: Reported net effort release and the nested monthly example are clearly scoped, but the underlying ledger, calculation, review deductions and approvals remain unavailable.
A5: A defined assurance-team need is described, yet there is no measured stakeholder satisfaction, assurance outcome or service-user benefit.
editorial_fixes: Correct the sentence "The account narrative describes training associates then working on the account and established reusable prompts" to "The account narrative describes training the associates then working on the account and establishing reusable prompts." This is the only material residual wording defect.
missing_evidence: Pulse task ledger, calculation method, review deductions and approval provenance for the 257 person-days.
Matched pre/post quality evidence for AI-assisted test artefacts and retained quality at lower effort.
Defined population, numerator, denominator and period for the reported 85% activity coverage.
Deployed-model identity, representative runs and an independent baseline-versus-adapted-model evaluation.
Stakeholder satisfaction or verified assurance and service-user outcomes.

reasons: N1: N01 substantiates workload volume and automated detection of explicit P90 failures, but four displayed samples per transaction and no passing closure record prevent a higher result.
N2: Production-informed design, six profiles, Kubernetes behaviours and abnormal cache reproduction provide strong representative-condition coverage, with primary run evidence still incomplete.
N3: Testing is credibly connected to risk detection and reported release and migration decisions; dates, acceptance records, reruns and observation windows are missing.
N4: Goals, roles, resources and reusable assets are specific, while the main efficiency, capacity and release achievements remain attributed narrative claims.
N5: Rebuild constraints, invalid exits, cache behaviour and missing telemetry are evaluated with concrete technical responses; quantitative remediation closure is still absent.
missing_evidence: Primary workload runs with transaction mix, sample populations, environment comparability and complete acceptance results.
Matched cache baseline and retest measurements with equivalent workload, change identifier and reviewer acceptance.
Before/after timings, run count, period, review effort and exceptions for each reported greater-than-90% effort reduction.
Release dates, readiness sign-offs, defect closure and defined post-release observation windows.
Telemetry-gate rerun and reconciled endpoint-level versus aggregate performance results.

reasons: I1: Domain-owned scenarios with centrally governed shared execution are a credible advancement in operating practice, but active use and comparative benefit are not verified.
I2: The driver, ownership model, tagging convention, generator and three-pipeline design are coherent and traceable to S02; implementation records were not inspected.
I3: The final paper substantiates an attempted transferable multi-team ownership and execution model and does not rely on external adoption as the sole test; evidence of effect remains limited.
I4: Goals, responsibilities and described assets are clear, but five-team participation, implementation and achieved benefits lack contribution and execution records.
I5: Maintenance, setup, triage and execution constraints receive plausible design responses; no completed failure-to-owner-to-rerun example demonstrates the response in operation.
missing_evidence: Contribution history, tagged-test inventory and shared-suite run records for the five described teams.
Repository and execution evidence for the template utility and three pipelines.
An end-to-end triage example from contributed-test failure through ownership, correction and successful rerun.
Like-for-like setup timings if an onboarding-efficiency claim is later introduced.
Measured change in duplicate maintenance, regression coverage, cross-service defect discovery or performance against the prior model.

council_recommendation: The final papers have corrected the material attribution, scope and overclaiming problems. Evidence is unchanged, so the remaining limitation is a primary-evidence plateau rather than an editorial one. AI scores 11/25 and still lacks measured quality and stakeholder outcomes. NFT scores 17/25 and remains strongest, but release, efficiency and remediation results require primary records. Innovation scores 14/25: its attempted industry contribution is now stated defensibly, while implementation, adoption and comparative benefit remain unverified. None meets 4/5 on every criterion. Make the single AI grammar correction; otherwise further rewriting will not materially improve substantiation. Preserve the separation between account AI, specialist applications, PerfOps and shared regression.
